title: Story
description: One story, account or teaching about resolving disputes, making peace or restoring relationships, as a Native nation or its people tell it, with every known telling. A telling cites its own published source record directly, or a private contributor filing. The project never retells a story in its own words: the record quotes the telling exactly, as far as the rights allow, and otherwise points to it. Stored as content/stories/<first letter of id, or _other>/<id>.yaml (decision record 0019).

id.description: Must equal the file name. Name the nation and the story, e.g. onondaga-nation-two-row-wampum.

title.description: The title the nation or publisher gives the story. Where none is given, a plain description in brackets, e.g. '[Account of the peace between the two clans]'.

titles_in_language.description: Titles or names in the nation's language, exactly as the source spells them.

nations.description: Tribe profile ids of the nations whose story this is. A story shared by several nations (such as a confederacy) lists each nation whose own telling is cited. Native Hawaiian stories use the native-hawaiian-community profile; Native Hawaiians are not a tribe.

community.description: A band, clan, town, village or other community within the nation, where the source names one.

kind.description: Open vocabulary. Suggested: traditional-story, historical-account (a recorded event such as a treaty or peace between peoples), teaching (a statement of values or law), court-opinion (a Tribal court opinion that tells or relies on a story), oral-history, essay, program-story (a story a peacemaking program tells about itself), other.

length.description: Of the longest telling cited. short: under about 1,500 words.

excerpts.description: The story in the nation's or teller's own words, quoted exactly from a telling, with a pinpoint. The project does not retell or summarize stories. Without permission an excerpt is a short passage (50 words or fewer) and only where the telling's permitted_uses allow quotation; otherwise the exact words are kept privately and the record carries only the pinpoint and fingerprint. The whole story is reproduced in full_text instead, and only where no permission is needed or permission was given (decision record 0034).

locator.description: Where in the telling: page, section, paragraph or the words it begins with.

text.description: The exact words, unchanged except for whitespace. Present only when the telling's permitted_uses level is quote or publish-in-full.

held_privately.description: True when the exact words are kept in the project's private files (for example a Tribal law, a court opinion, or a publisher that asks to be asked first) and not in the repository.

words.description: Number of words in the exact excerpt.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact excerpt (UTF-8, NFC, whitespace collapsed to single spaces), so a private excerpt can be checked without publishing it.

full_text.description: The whole story in the teller's exact words, as one telling prints it, shown on the story's page (decision record 0034). Only where no permission is needed or permission was given: a public-domain telling, a nation's own law that the site serves under decision record 0031, or a telling whose permitted_uses level is publish-in-full. Never a retelling: every paragraph is the source's own text, and anything left out is marked where it was.

locator.description: Where in the telling the text runs: pages, section, or the words it begins and ends with.

basis.description: public-domain: the telling's source record has rights basis public-domain (for example a book published in the United States before 1931, or a work of the United States government). nation-law: the telling is a nation's own law, served on the site under decision record 0031. permission: the telling's permitted_uses level is publish-in-full.

basis_note.description: Why the full text may be shown, in a sentence.

transcribed_from.description: The copy the text was taken from and how it was checked against the printed page.

paragraphs.description: The text, one paragraph per item, unchanged except for whitespace, line-end hyphens and spaces the typesetter put before punctuation. An object marks a passage left out, where it was.

omitted.description: What kind of passage is left out and why, in a sentence, without describing its content.

locator.description: Where the passage is in the telling, so a reader can find it.

notes.description: Transcription notes shown under the text, such as a letter damaged in the printing.

words.description: Number of words in the paragraphs that are text.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the text paragraphs joined by a blank line (UTF-8, NFC, whitespace in each paragraph collapsed to single spaces).

topics.description: Free tags, e.g. peace-between-nations, making-amends, family-dispute, role-of-elders, origin-of-a-court.

tellings.description: Every known telling, the nation's own first. Each cites one published source record (`source`) or one private contributor filing (`filing`), never both.

protocols.description: Cultural protocols that govern the story, stated by the nation or its people. Record only what a source says; never infer a protocol.

kind.description: seasonal: told only in a season. setting: told only in a place or setting. teller: only certain people may tell it. clan-owned or family-owned: the story is the property of a clan or family. name-avoidance: a name is not spoken outside ceremony or at all. permission-required: the source asks to be contacted before reuse.

statement.description: What the source says, in the project's words or a short quotation.

source.description: Source record that states the protocol.

how_the_project_follows_it.description: e.g. 'shown only from November to February', 'personal name not used'.

access.description: Access for the story as a whole: the most restrictive level among its tellings and protocols. On the website, a nation-review-first story is shown with a notice that the nation has not reviewed it, and a telling from a contributor filing only once it is public (decision record 0029).

anthology.description: Whether the story could appear in full in a book or anthology, and whose permission that would take.

reason.description: Why it is or is not a candidate (project analysis).

telling.description: Id of the telling that would be reprinted.

permission_from.description: Each permission a reprint needs. Copyright and cultural authority are asked separately even when one office holds both.

holder.description: Role, office or publisher, never a private person's contact details.

status.description: The request's trail is kept in the cited source's rights log, or in the contributor filing.

id.description: Unique within the record, e.g. nation-website-2024.

source.description: Key of the source record for this telling, cited directly: the page, opinion, book or recording where the nation or teller published it.

filing.description: Private contributor filing, for a story that reached the project from a person rather than a publication.

as_of.description: When this telling was published or told.

teller.description: The teller or author, credited as the source or contributor gives it.

published_by.description: Who published this telling, e.g. 'Onondaga Nation', 'Chickasaw Press'.

authority.description: Whose voice this telling is. The nation's own channels come first. outside-recorder (an anthropologist, journalist or government writer) is kept only when important, and never as the only telling of a story the nation tells itself.
